sourceCheck: Verified the official study guide, exam page and certification page on 2026-10-08. The guide shows Skills measured as of April 17, 2026 and one outline version. The four skill areas, weights 25–30%, 20–25%, 15–20% and 30–35%, all twelve skill groups and their bullets match the request; no wording, weight or group differences were found. The change log lists a minor audience-profile change. AZ-305 remains the required exam; its page shows Retirement date: none and the April 17, 2026 English update. No newer outline or certification retirement notice appears. The certification confirms Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate as its prerequisite. Reviewed AZ-305T00-A, the four supplied learning paths, the Azure Architecture Center, the Azure Well-Architected Framework and the current Cloud Adoption Framework. Confirmed product exclusions: Azure Blueprints is in phased retirement toward January 31, 2027; Azure AD B2C is unavailable to new purchasers; Microsoft Entra Permissions Management and the Log Analytics agent are retired; Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard and Premium retire September 30, 2028, and Enterprise and Enterprise Flash retire March 31, 2027; Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is on a retirement path; Azure Spring Apps is in its retirement period; Azure Front Door (classic) retires March 31, 2027; Application Gateway V1 is retired; non-AZ VPN Gateway SKUs are slated for migration; kubenet retires March 31, 2028 and Azure CNI Node Subnet is legacy; Data Migration Assistant and Movere are retired; Fsv2 retired October 1, 2026; Intel SGX enclave support ends October 31, 2027; Azure Synapse Link for Cosmos DB is deprecated; Azure Synapse Analytics Data Explorer is retired. Current checks confirm Key Vault's RBAC default beginning with API version 2026-02-01 and Cloud Sync's documented device synchronization. Azure Data Factory remains current. Preview exclusions include grouped-control Regulatory Compliance, multi-stage DCR transformations, standard service endpoint, Hyperscale auto-pause and multiple failover-group secondaries. Application Gateway's TCP/TLS proxy page has no Preview label. Linux Consumption documentation retains the legacy/retirement wording discrepancy, so it is excluded. The documented contradictions concerning SQL tier defaults, Cosmos DB restore targets, object replication with storage failover and failover-group secondary regions remain outside the plan.

cards.statement: Azure Monitor collects resource logs automatically when an Azure resource starts generating them.
cards.explanation: Azure Monitor resource logs need a diagnostic setting for collection. Include log routing in the design before relying on these logs for troubleshooting.
cards.misconception: Resource logs are collected automatically as soon as a resource emits them.

source.title: Resource logs in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Azure Monitor diagnostic settings can route resource logs through Azure Event Hubs to a non-Microsoft SIEM.
cards.explanation: Azure Event Hubs provides the documented streaming destination for sending Azure Monitor resource logs to external SIEM systems.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Diagnostic settings support central log routing to a workspace in another subscription with suitable access.
cards.explanation: A diagnostic setting may target another subscription when its configuring user has appropriate access to both. This supports centralized logging across subscriptions.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Diagnostic settings can preserve metric dimensions when exporting platform metrics to a Log Analytics workspace.
cards.explanation: Diagnostic settings flatten multidimensional metrics and aggregate across dimension values. Use another collection path when the analysis needs that breakdown.
cards.misconception: Diagnostic exports retain the dimensional breakdown available in native metrics.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: A Log Analytics workspace stores incoming logs in the region of the resource that emits them.
cards.explanation: Log data resides in the workspace's region. Choose the workspace location to meet the workload's data residency requirements.
cards.misconception: Workspace data stays in the source resource's region regardless of the workspace location.

source.title: Design a Log Analytics workspace architecture

cards.statement: Resource-context access can isolate teams' resource logs within a shared Log Analytics workspace.
cards.explanation: Resource-context access limits a resource owner's queries to logs for resources they can access. A shared workspace can therefore serve separate application teams.

source.title: Design a Log Analytics workspace architecture

cards.statement: Basic tables in Azure Monitor Logs support simple log alerts for data that needs occasional investigation.
cards.explanation: The Basic plan reduces ingestion cost for medium-touch logs while supporting simple log alerts. It suits data retained for occasional troubleshooting.
cards.volatilityNote: Table-plan query and alert capabilities are evolving.

source.title: Azure Monitor Logs overview

cards.statement: Auxiliary tables offer the same interactive query performance as Analytics tables in Azure Monitor Logs.
cards.explanation: Auxiliary queries are slower and suit low-touch audit or compliance data. Analytics provides optimized query performance for frequent operational analysis.
cards.misconception: Auxiliary provides Analytics-level query performance at a lower ingestion cost.

source.title: Azure Monitor Logs overview

cards.statement: Azure Monitor Agent automatically applies updated collection rules associated with its virtual machine.
cards.explanation: Azure Monitor Agent periodically checks its associated data collection rules for updates. Central rules keep collection consistent across a fleet.

source.title: Azure Monitor Agent overview

cards.statement: A DCR ingestion filter lets Log Analytics users recover excluded records by changing a query.
cards.explanation: An ingestion-time transformation filters records before workspace storage. A later Log Analytics query cannot recover records excluded from that ingestion path.
cards.misconception: An ingestion filter behaves like a reversible query filter over retained raw data.

source.title: Transformations in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Application Insights lets telemetry senders authenticate with a connection string's instrumentation key.
cards.explanation: The instrumentation key identifies an Application Insights resource; it is not a security credential. Authenticated telemetry ingestion uses Microsoft Entra ID.
cards.misconception: The instrumentation key authenticates the application sending telemetry.

source.title: Connection strings in Application Insights

cards.statement: Application Insights' custom OpenTelemetry sampler keeps complete traces while reducing telemetry volume.
cards.explanation: Application Insights relies on the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry sampler to retain complete traces and reduce broken diagnostic traces during sampling.

source.title: Sampling in Azure Monitor Application Insights with OpenTelemetry

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication checks on-premises sign-in hours when validating passwords.
cards.explanation: Pass-through authentication validates credentials against on-premises Active Directory at sign-in. It enforces the directory's permitted sign-in hours at that point.

source.title: Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution

cards.statement: Pass-through authentication automatically switches to password hash synchronization during an on-premises outage.
cards.explanation: Administrators manually switch pass-through authentication to password hash synchronization. Prepare synchronization before an on-premises outage.
cards.misconception: Enabling password hash synchronization makes authentication failover automatic.

source.title: Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution

cards.statement: Federation supports cloud sign-in with sAMAccountName when an organization retains DOMAIN\username logins.
cards.explanation: A requirement to use sAMAccountName, such as DOMAIN\username, calls for federated authentication. Microsoft Entra ID's native hybrid sign-in options use other supported identifiers.

source.title: Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra External ID uses an external tenant for B2B guests who access employee applications.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Entra External ID places B2B collaboration guests in the workforce tenant containing employee applications. An external tenant serves consumer and business-customer applications.
cards.misconception: Business collaboration guests belong in an external tenant because they are external users.

source.title: Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID

cards.statement: A user-assigned managed identity lets replacement virtual machines reuse the same authorized identity.
cards.explanation: A user-assigned managed identity exists independently of the virtual machines using it. Replacing those machines preserves the identity and its permissions.

source.title: What is managed identities for Azure resources?

cards.statement: A custom Azure RBAC role can span subscriptions that trust different Microsoft Entra tenants.
cards.explanation: A custom Azure RBAC role can be shared across subscriptions that trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant. Separate tenants need their own role definitions.
cards.misconception: A custom role definition is portable across subscriptions regardless of their tenant.

source.title: Azure custom roles

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access trusts B2B guests' home-tenant MFA claims by default.
cards.explanation: Initial cross-tenant access settings exclude trust in another tenant's MFA claims. Administrators enable inbound MFA trust to let those claims satisfy their Conditional Access policies.
cards.misconception: A guest's successful home-tenant MFA automatically satisfies the resource tenant's MFA requirement.

source.title: Overview: Cross-tenant access with Microsoft Entra External ID

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra application proxy uses Kerberos constrained delegation for single sign-on to IWA apps.
cards.explanation: For web applications using Integrated Windows Authentication, the private network connector uses Kerberos constrained delegation to authenticate users to the application.

source.title: Microsoft Entra application proxy

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra Domain Services can extend an on-premises domain with Microsoft-managed domain controllers.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services creates a standalone managed domain. It offers legacy domain protocols for Azure workloads rather than extending the existing on-premises domain.
cards.misconception: The managed domain controllers become additional controllers in the existing on-premises domain.

source.title: What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends Azure RBAC for Azure Key Vault data-plane access to secrets, keys and certificates.
cards.explanation: Azure RBAC centralizes Azure Key Vault access and separates permission management from vault administration. Microsoft recommends it over the legacy access policy model.

source.title: Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) vs. access policies (legacy)

cards.statement: Azure Key Vault supports built-in automatic renewal for certificates from a nonintegrated certificate authority.
cards.explanation: Certificates from a nonintegrated certificate authority need an external signing and merge process for renewal. Azure Key Vault provides expiration notifications for them.
cards.misconception: Importing a certificate gives Key Vault built-in renewal integration with its issuing authority.

source.title: Renew your Azure Key Vault certificates

cards.statement: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM isolates a customer's keys with a customer-specific security domain.
cards.explanation: Each Azure Key Vault Managed HSM instance has a dedicated HSM cluster and its own security domain. This creates cryptographic isolation for the customer's keys.

source.title: What is Azure Key Vault Managed HSM?

cards.statement: A management-group Azure Policy assignment reaches subscriptions nested beneath that management group.
cards.explanation: A management-group policy assignment governs descendant subscriptions and their resources, giving an organization a common governance baseline.

source.title: What are Azure management groups?

cards.statement: A management group can govern subscriptions that trust different Microsoft Entra tenants together.
cards.explanation: Subscriptions in a management group trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant. A cross-tenant organization needs a governance design that respects that boundary.
cards.misconception: Management groups provide a single hierarchy across Microsoft Entra tenants.

source.title: What are Azure management groups?

cards.statement: An application database can stay in a separate resource group from a web app with a different lifecycle.
cards.explanation: Azure resources in separate resource groups can connect to one another. This lets a long-lived database follow a different deployment and deletion lifecycle from its web app.

source.title: What is Azure Resource Manager?

cards.statement: A resource-group cost-center tag automatically labels the group's resources for resource-level chargeback.
cards.explanation: Resource-group tags stay on the group. Resource-level cost allocation needs tags on the resources or a deliberate tagging policy.
cards.misconception: Resource group tags automatically propagate to contained resources.

source.title: Use tags to organize your Azure resources and management hierarchy

cards.statement: Azure Policy automatically applies additions to an initiative through its existing assignments.
cards.explanation: When an architect adds policy definitions to an initiative, its existing assignments include them. Teams can expand a governance baseline while keeping its assignment structure.

source.title: Overview of Azure Policy

cards.statement: An Azure Policy exemption can end a temporary waiver automatically on its scheduled expiration date.
cards.explanation: A policy exemption records an accepted compliance exception. At its expiration, Azure Policy stops honoring the waiver while retaining the exemption object for records.

source.title: Azure Policy exemption structure

cards.statement: Azure Policy stops evaluating a deployed resource after its initial compliance assessment completes.
cards.explanation: Azure Policy reassesses resource compliance after resource updates and during regular compliance scans. A deployment-time result is a starting point for ongoing governance.
cards.misconception: Policy compliance evaluation ends after the initial assessment.

source.title: Overview of Azure Policy

cards.statement: A custom Azure Policy definition in one subscription supports assignments in a separate subscription.
cards.explanation: A custom policy definition stored in a subscription is available for assignments within that subscription. A separate subscription falls outside its definition scope.
cards.misconception: The definition location has no effect on where a custom policy can be assigned.

source.title: Understand scope in Azure Policy

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management supports approval before eligible users activate Azure resource roles.
cards.explanation: Privileged Identity Management can hold an eligible Azure resource role activation for a designated approver's decision, giving architects a human approval gate for elevated access.

source.title: Configure Azure resource role settings in Privileged Identity Management

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra access reviews directly remove denied members from groups synchronized from on-premises.
cards.explanation: Access review results leave membership in on-premises-origin groups unchanged. Administrators need a process that applies denied membership decisions in the source directory.
cards.misconception: Applying access review results changes membership in synchronized on-premises groups.

source.title: Complete an access review of groups and applications in access reviews

cards.statement: Different request policies in one entitlement management access package can grant different resource roles.
cards.explanation: Access package policies vary eligibility, approval and lifecycle settings. Users assigned the package receive its resource roles, so different role bundles need different packages.
cards.misconception: Each request policy in an access package selects a different resource-role bundle.

source.title: Create an access package in entitlement management

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra lifecycle workflows can invoke Azure Logic Apps to perform custom employee offboarding tasks.
cards.explanation: Lifecycle workflows use custom task extensions to run Azure Logic Apps when employee lifecycle requirements extend beyond built-in tasks.

source.title: Lifecycle Workflows custom task extension

cards.statement: Azure SQL Managed Instance supports native cross-database queries between databases on the same instance.
cards.explanation: Native cross-database queries within an instance let an existing application retain this SQL Server dependency in a managed service.

source.title: What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?

cards.statement: SQL Server on Azure VMs lets administrators install OS-level agents directly on the database host.
cards.explanation: SQL Server on Azure VMs gives administrators control of the guest operating system, meeting requirements for custom software on the database host.

source.title: What is Azure SQL?

cards.statement: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server supports built-in PgBouncer on the Burstable tier.
cards.explanation: Built-in PgBouncer is available in the General Purpose and Memory Optimized compute tiers. A Burstable design needs a different connection-pooling solution.
cards.misconception: Built-in connection pooling is available across the flexible server compute tiers.
tags: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
cards.volatilityNote: The compute tiers that include built-in PgBouncer may expand.

source.title: PgBouncer in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database supports reservation discounts for databases that use the DTU purchasing model.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database reservations apply to the vCore purchasing model. A DTU database design does not qualify for this compute discount.
cards.misconception: Reservation discounts apply equally to the DTU and vCore purchasing models.

source.title: vCore purchasing model - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database serverless can bill active idle databases for less compute than their configured minimum.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database serverless applies the configured minimum vCores and memory to compute billing while the database remains active, even when demand falls below those levels.
cards.misconception: Serverless billing follows low utilization below the configured minimum while a database stays active.

source.title: Serverless compute tier for Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database elastic pools share compute among databases whose workload peaks occur at different times.
cards.explanation: Databases with staggered demand reuse pooled compute, reducing the capacity otherwise reserved for separate peak-sized databases.

source.title: Manage multiple databases with elastic pools in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database General Purpose stores persistent data files separately from its compute nodes.
cards.explanation: General Purpose keeps database files in remote Azure Blob storage. Storage latency therefore matters when evaluating a workload for this tier.

source.title: vCore purchasing model - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database Business Critical supports In-Memory OLTP tables for transaction-heavy applications.
cards.explanation: The Business Critical tier includes In-Memory OLTP support, so a design that depends on memory-optimized tables can retain that capability.

source.title: In-memory technologies in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database Hyperscale ties a named replica's compute size to the primary replica's compute size.
cards.explanation: A Hyperscale named replica has its own service level objective. Architects size its compute independently for the read workload it serves.
cards.misconception: Named replicas inherit the primary replica's compute sizing.

source.title: Hyperscale secondary replicas

cards.statement: Always Encrypted grants Azure SQL Database administrators plaintext access through database permissions alone.
cards.explanation: Always Encrypted separates database administration from key access. Reading protected column values also needs access to the column master key outside the database.
cards.misconception: Database administrator permissions are sufficient to decrypt Always Encrypted columns.

source.title: Always Encrypted

cards.statement: Dynamic data masking can hide Azure SQL Database query results from users in the db_owner database role.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database users in db_owner see original values despite dynamic data masking. Masking limits exposure to nonprivileged users.
cards.misconception: Dynamic data masking protects column plaintext from database owners.

source.title: Dynamic data masking

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database enables TDE with a service-managed key by default for new empty databases.
cards.explanation: New empty Azure SQL databases use service-managed transparent data encryption by default, protecting database files and logs against offline access.

source.title: Transparent data encryption for SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, and Azure Synapse Analytics
